title: Eribulin · Days 1 and 8 of 21

agents.name: Eribulin
agents.explanation: Eribulin blocks growth of the tiny structures cells need to divide. It can slow cancer growth, but can also affect blood cells and nerves.
agents.watch: Report numbness, weakness or difficulty with walking or hand tasks before the next dose. Fever or sudden illness needs immediate advice; palpitations or fainting need urgent assessment.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and sepsis
Numbness, tingling or weakness, sometimes lasting
Fatigue, hair loss, nausea and constipation
Changes to heart rhythm / QT in susceptible people

phases_title: Treatment, reassessment and the next decision
phases_note: This card describes one active chemotherapy schedule. There is no automatic maintenance phase; continuing, changing or stopping treatment follows clinical review.
timeline_note: Treatment markers show the planned days. Symptom bands show broad possibilities, not measured risk curves or guaranteed symptom-free days.
safety_note: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell needs prompt advice on any day, including planned treatment-free weeks.
teachback: Which days are treatment days, what checks are due before the next dose, and who is arranging and reviewing the next scan?
consent_support: Discuss the exact indication, expected benefit, alternatives, uncertainty, serious and lasting risks, contraception and fertility, venous access, monitoring and the urgent contact plan. EU dose labels use eribulin base. 1.23 mg/m² base corresponds to 1.4 mg/m² mesylate in some trial reports; these are not two alternative doses.
urgent_extra: New chest pain, fainting, severe breathlessness, fever or sudden illness needs urgent assessment. Report worsening numbness, severe constipation, mouth ulcers or inability to drink promptly.

questions.q: Which treatment days and breaks should I expect?
questions.a: Eribulin on Days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. Day 15 is a planned treatment-free week. Treatment continues while beneficial and tolerated.

questions.q: When do I need blood tests, an ECG or echo?
questions.a: FBC, renal and liver profile before starting and at the start of each cycle. The EMA product information specifies FBC before every dose, including Day 8; additional renal / liver tests follow clinical need. ECG before starting and during treatment when there is cardiac disease, a slow / abnormal rhythm, QT-prolonging medicines or electrolyte disturbance. Correct low potassium, calcium or magnesium before treatment; repeat monitoring follows risk and findings. No fixed routine echo interval is specified for eribulin alone. Cardiac symptoms or risk prompt individual assessment. If trastuzumab is separately prescribed, use its own cardiac-monitoring plan.

questions.q: When will we know whether treatment is helping?
questions.a: For metastatic breast cancer, ESMO recommends response evaluation generally every 2–4 months, adjusted to disease, treatment and symptoms. Agree the scan type, due window and result-review appointment; symptoms can prompt earlier assessment. For the other cancer indications on this card, use the cancer-specific monitoring plan; the breast interval is not transferred automatically.

questions.q: Where do surgery or radiotherapy fit?
questions.a: These are advanced-disease regimens. Surgery or radiotherapy is used only for a defined local or symptom-control purpose. The oncology and radiation teams decide whether chemotherapy continues, pauses or precedes radiation; no routine overlap is implied.
Tumour markers, when useful for the cancer being treated, supplement clinical assessment and imaging. A marker result alone should not determine treatment failure or a treatment change.

questions.q: Does a port mean a pump at home?
questions.a: No. A port is a route into a vein. Staff disconnect the infusion and remove the port needle after the visit when appropriate; removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure.

evidence.title: EMBRACE: eribulin Days 1 and 8 every 21 days
evidence.intro: Evidence belongs to the cancer, population and schedule actually studied.
evidence.population: 762 women with heavily pretreated locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer; 2-5 prior chemotherapy regimens, at least two for advanced disease, including anthracycline and taxane unless contraindicated.
evidence.interpretation: Randomized phase III evidence supports this 21-day eribulin schedule in the studied advanced-breast population; median overall survival was 13.1 versus 10.6 months against physician's-choice treatment (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.66-0.99). Population-level historical trial results are not an individual prognosis, do not establish benefit in every line/subtype, and must not be copied to the 28-day schedule or liposarcoma. Trials report 1.4 mg/m² eribulin mesylate; the Irish/EU product dose is expressed as 1.23 mg/m² eribulin base. Never substitute the numeric dose expression without checking formulation.

items.title: Indication
items.text: Advanced breast cancer after at least one chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease, with prior anthracycline and taxane unless unsuitable; or adult unresectable liposarcoma after anthracycline unless unsuitable.

items.title: Dose and formulation
items.text: 1.23 mg/m² eribulin base. EU dose labels use eribulin base. 1.23 mg/m² base corresponds to 1.4 mg/m² mesylate in some trial reports; these are not two alternative doses.

items.title: Evidence limits

Population-level historical trial results are not an individual prognosis, do not establish benefit in every line/subtype, and must not be copied to the 28-day schedule or liposarcoma. Trials report 1.4 mg/m² eribulin mesylate; the Irish/EU product dose is expressed as 1.23 mg/m² eribulin base. Never substitute the numeric dose expression without checking formulation.

items.title: Eribulin versus dacarbazine: advanced liposarcoma evidence
items.text: 452 adults with advanced liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after at least two systemic regimens including anthracycline, using Days 1 and 8 every 21 days. Separate sarcoma trial and its liposarcoma subgroup support the liposarcoma indication; breast-trial benefit figures do not apply. The licensed liposarcoma indication must not be expanded to all sarcomas because the parent trial also enrolled leiomyosarcoma. Use current NCCP eligibility and EMA indication wording. Do not apply breast imaging or CA15-3/CEA pathways to liposarcoma.

chronology_notes.title: A delay changes the treatment plan
chronology_notes.text: Do not move, double or make up doses yourself. A delayed infusion does not automatically move an already-due scan or heart test.

chronology_notes.title: Review milestone
chronology_notes.text: Review symptoms and benefit throughout each cycle; arrange cancer-specific response imaging under the agreed plan.

logistics.title: Your infusion and access plan
logistics.intro: Eribulin on Days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. Day 15 is a planned treatment-free week. Treatment continues while beneficial and tolerated.

steps.title: Before the first visit
steps.text: Confirm the indication, baseline bloods, required cardiac checks, medicines review and consent before the first infusion.

steps.title: Plan venous access
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions.

steps.title: Infusion day
steps.text: Eribulin is given by IV infusion over 5 minutes; blood review, preparation and access make the full visit longer. Staff observe for reactions. Report burning, pain, swelling or leakage at the infusion site immediately.

steps.title: Home and next review
steps.text: This regimen does not routinely need a take-home infusion pump. Staff disconnect the infusion; a port is de-accessed when appropriate. Keep line-care and next-visit instructions.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.

details.title: Visit length
details.text: Eribulin is given by IV infusion over 5 minutes; blood review, preparation and access make the full visit longer. A port is optional access, not a requirement for a take-home pump. This regimen has no routine ambulatory pump.

details.title: Premedication
details.text: No routine hypersensitivity premedication is specified. Low-risk antiemetic support is reviewed separately, including QT interactions.

anatomy: Report numbness, tingling, weakness or loss of function.
